members.title: EA关闭BioWare，《质量效应》新作被砍
EA closes Mass Effect, Dragon Age creator BioWare after 30 years of game development
BioWare is closing after 30 years
BREAKING: BioWare Is Shutting Down

news.body:
【更新】BioWare 就关闭一事发布声明。工作室表示，过去三十多年里，这里一直是讲故事的人、开发者和玩家的家园。一代代BioWare员工共同创造的成果值得庆祝，也值得铭记。正是因为玩家游玩这些游戏、为其中的抉择争论、爱上游戏角色，并让这些世界成为自己的世界，这些游戏才有了超越游戏本身的意义。
工作室最后代表全体员工感谢玩家，称他们是 BioWare 故事中最有意义的部分。
【原文】美国艺电公司（EA）宣布将裁员约400人，并关闭旗下开发过《龙腾世纪》和《质量效应》的老牌游戏工作室 BioWare 。此次裁员规模约占 EA 总员工数的3%，其中包括BioWare约50名员工。作为调整的一部分，正处于早期开发阶段的《质量效应》新作已被取消。
EA 首席运营官David Tinson和首席工作室官 Cam Weber 在致员工的内部信中表示，公司在过去几个月审视了各项业务，并决定削减部分项目。
这家游戏巨头今年8月在沙特阿拉伯投资基金主导的550亿美元杠杆收购后转为私有制，背负了约180亿美元债务。此前，公司曾告知投资者计划通过削减研发成本等方式节省高达7亿美元开支。
BioWare于1995年创立，并在2007年被 EA 收购。该工作室曾推出多部热门角色扮演游戏，但近年来的《质量效应：仙女座》和《圣歌》等作品反响平平。其最新作品《龙腾世纪：影障守护者》销量未达预期，EA 去年已对该工作室进行了大幅精简。
EA 表示，未来将继续投资体育游戏、《Apex英雄》以及动作冒险项目，包括下一部《星球大战 绝地》游戏和一款以漫威钢铁侠为主角的新作。公司还将继续推进《战地》系列，而旗下Respawn与DICE工作室将合作开发新项目，这很可能是《星球大战：前线》系列的新作。
此前，EA 取消了一款代号为Project Lotus的《模拟人生》系列游戏，转而优先推进代号为Project Evergreen的项目。同时，滑板游戏《skate》将继续开发，但开发团队规模将会缩减。

是不是以为夜之城的故事已经结束了？这才哪儿到哪儿啊！
YT17
4 小时前
发布于
资讯
《赛博朋克2077》边缘行者 2｜版本更新 2.5 现已正式公布。在本次更新于本周正式登陆 PC、PlayStation 5 和 Xbox Series X|S 等平台之前，官方率先揭晓了内容详情。据悉，Nintendo Switch 2 和 Mac 平台的玩家将延后一些时间陆续收到更新。
官方表示，是不是以为夜之城的故事已经结束了？这才哪儿到哪儿啊！
边缘行者内容
添加了一个新的支线任务“连梦都被编了号”，内容发生在《赛博朋克：边缘行者 2》的剧情之前。解锁方式：完成“偷货”以及和歌子的两个委托，然后等待她的消息。
添加了以人物“国王”为原型的五件套装备，可以在支线任务“连梦都被编了号”期间获得。
添加了一个新的电台：扳机 102.0 FM，其中收录多首《赛博朋克：边缘行者》剧集的精选曲目。
秀出风采
全新的服装系列登陆夜之城！现在可以在特定服装商贩处购买 5 套新的穿搭：
麦西威码：在海伍德、河谷区、小唐人街上架
神宫寺：在市政中心上架
网络监察：在歌舞伎区、日本街上架
ICON 美国：在太平洲、恶土、北区上架
稍后还有一套服装也会在夜之城推出…
现在可以在歌舞伎区和日本街的服装商贩处购买新美国敌后人员套装。
现在可以通过 Twitch 掉宝获取古德拉 Turbo-R V-Tech 的 4 个新的调色通皮肤。
现在 V 可以使用部分之前 NPC 的专属发型。请注意，部分发型只适用于女性化或者男性化体型。
秀出你的义体！现在你可以自定义手掌义体。装备螳螂刀、大猩猩手臂、单分子线或者射弹发射系统，前往五家华彩医生的诊所之一（在地图上用喷漆图标标记），让义体焕然一新。每家华彩医生诊所都位于独特的店铺里，它们有自己专属的开场演出，附带了配音和动画，同时还能提供一系列能够自定义颜色的独特义体皮肤。
有时候一把枪确实不够。镇定技能树里添加了双倍麻烦专长（以及四个辅助专长），带来完全不一样的游戏玩法，让你可以双持动能类别的手枪和左轮手枪。
照片模式添加了《赛博朋克集换式卡牌游戏》的相框，让你把绝美的照片做成定制卡牌的样子。
照片模式添加了新姿势，展现你双持武器的英姿。
丰富的模组
添加了由 mod.io 提供的跨平台模组支持。你可以直接在游戏内菜单里方便地浏览和安装精选的玩家自制模组。而这只是迈向跨平台模组的第一步。未来还会发布更多模组。该功能现在已经在 PC、Mac、PlayStation 5、PlayStation 5 Pro 和 Xbox Series X|S 平台上推出。
游戏世界升级
欢迎来到天堂！
新增了一个支线任务。它将带你踏上解谜之旅，并且在理查德·奈特的解说下通过导览来探索夜之城。完成“偷货”任务并且街头声望达到 15 级后解锁。
夜之城各处添加了 12 张供玩家探索的小奥秘塔罗牌。塔罗牌菜单现在为大奥秘和小奥秘卡牌设置了不同的版块。新的塔罗牌属于新的支线任务的一部分，也是任务“山丘上的愚者”的扩展内容。扫描任意一张新卡牌就可以激活。集齐所有卡牌能够获得特殊奖励。
游戏体验
现在“读取游戏”菜单里的存档会按照不同的流程档单独分组。
为公寓和载具的储藏处添加了物品筛选功能。
现在“读取游戏”菜单里使用了模组的存档会带有专属图标。请注意，在主机上使用带有模组的存档进行游戏时无法获得成就或者奖杯。
为主机添加了视野（FOV）滑动条。
更新了 AMD FSR 选项。FSR 3 升级技术不再包含在内，但是 FSR 2.1、FSR 4 和 FSR 3.1 帧生成功能依然可用。
更新了 CD PROJEKT RED 帐户绑定、我的奖励和自动记录同意菜单。
技术
添加了对 DLSS 4.5 的支持，包括最高 6X 的多帧生成或者动态多帧生成，以及第二代 Transformer 模型。
添加了在兼容的三星 Odyssey 3D 显示器上对裸眼 3D 效果的支持，以及可以在 3D 深度和观看舒适度之间进行平衡的动态舒适设置。
添加了在 Mac 上对 MetalFX 帧插值和降噪的支持。
在设置中添加了 FSR Anti-Lag 2 的开关选项。
加入了各种性能优化，包括专门针对光线追踪和 PlayStation 5 Pro 的改善。
改善了 HDR 渲染，在兼容的显示器上提供更准确的颜色、亮度和对比度。
修正
修正了一个在 Nintendo Switch 2 上保存游戏可能会出现“保存失败：空间不足”错误的问题。
修正了一个在 PlayStation 5 上调整 HDR 设置没有效果的问题。
只身打马
- 修正了一个德拉曼出租车撞上其它载具后会卡住，导致任务进度无法推进的问题。
修正了一个启用胶片颗粒没有效果的问题。
修正了一个在使用特定控制方案时，扫描过程中标记敌人会让 V 蹲伏或者起身的问题。
修正了一个第三人称镜头的控制器设置缺失的问题。
修正了各种语言的多个错字。
为版本更新 2.1 之后加入的功能和内容添加了各种其它修正。

四人联机探索火星地底！《无光绝境》合作测试开启，预计12 月 2 日上线抢先体验
由 Pokuch 开发、META Publishing 发行的开放世界生存冒险游戏《无光绝境》（Blind Descent），已于10月14日开启多人合作 Playtest。本次测试以联机体验为重点，支持最多四人共同游玩。玩家可通过 Steam 商店页面申请免费测试资格。
本轮测试重点开放多人合作
与此前的单人测试相比，本轮 Playtest 加入了多人合作体验。玩家可以与朋友进入同一场冒险，一起收集资源、制作工具、建立生存据点，并继续探索地下区域
多人模式下，探索与生存需要队伍共同安排。成员可以分工准备物资、研究材料用途，也可以结伴推进，在遭遇陌生生物或环境危险时互相协助。本次测试为玩家提供了实际体验合作玩法的机会，开发团队也将根据反馈继续调整游戏
在外星生态中探索、制作与适应
游戏将场景设定在火星地表之下。玩家在寻找失踪探险队线索的过程中，会接触到一个具有独特生物与环境的地下生态系统。观察周围的生命形态、理解资源用途，是推进探索的一部分。
生存制作也与这一过程相联系。玩家需要收集材料，通过研究与尝试制作工具，为后续探索准备条件，并逐步建立能够落脚和补给的据点。
此外，变异是游戏适应机制的一部分。角色可以通过与地下生态系统发生交互产生变化，尝试与环境共生；也可以依靠科学、工具和设备应对生存压力。上述为游戏的整体玩法方向，具体可体验内容以本轮测试版本为准。
测试参与方式
测试自10月14日开放，预计持续两周。目前，Steam 商店页面设有“加入Playtest”入口。玩家登录 Steam 后，可点击“请求访问权限”提交申请，获得资格后下载测试客户端，具体申请地址：https://store.steampowered.com/app/1209970
《无光绝境》计划于2026年12月2日推出抢先体验版本。

members.title: 《魔域》金秋幻兽「澜境君·镜汐」全爆料：上线时间、至臻榜单、灵蕴获取与助战玩法

news.body:
《魔域》金秋幻兽「澜境君·镜汐」是2026年全新金秋幻兽，正式服于10月23日维护后上线，先锋区提前至10月21日维护后上线。本文围绕镜汐的上线时间、至臻榜单排名规则、灵蕴获取方式、技能结构以及助战玩法，梳理官网已公布的完整机制信息。
上线时间与活动周期：先锋区与正式服有两天时间差
镜汐在正式服于10月23日维护后上线，先锋区提前两天，为10月21日维护后上线。专属福利活动「聚灵返臻」的周期随区服不同而不同：正式服为10月23日维护后至11月24日21:59，先锋区为10月21日维护后至11月22日21:59。两个区服的上线节点和活动截止时间均相差两天，参与活动的玩家需要按所在区服的时间安排养成与投喂节奏。
至臻榜单规则：3000分登记，按投喂灵蕴数量排名
镜汐达到3000分时即可登记参与至臻榜单角逐。至臻榜单的排名依据是镜汐被投喂的灵蕴数量，而非评分高低或战力数值。系统根据排名发放光效、称号卡、外套包等奖励，并有专属道具可焕新镜汐外观与技能特效。这里需要区分两个规则：3000分是参与登记的准入门槛，投喂灵蕴数量决定最终排名，二者不是同一个条件。
灵蕴获取与流转：1500分以上产出，求购获得，可出售
灵蕴是至臻榜单排名的核心资源，获取方式有两种。第一种是自我产出：1500分及以上的镜汐每24小时可产出一定数量灵蕴，评分越高产出越多。第二种是玩家间流转：通过游戏内发布求购信息从其他勇士处获得灵蕴。如果勇士手上有多余灵蕴，可前往「聚灵返臻」活动界面进行出售。灵蕴的产出、求购与出售构成一个闭环，玩家可根据自身镜汐的评分和榜单竞争情况选择获取路径。
技能结构：1个主动、6个被动、4个专属非战技能
镜汐共有1个主动技能、6个被动技能以及4个专属非战技能，提升伤害与各项增益的同时，还提供专属坐骑、击杀效果和炫耀技能。
主动技能为「水镜破魔」：以宝镜幻化出彩池澜境，镜汐从宝镜中跃出，对范围内敌人进行多次攻击造成多段伤害，最后额外造成一定固定伤害。
6个被动技能分别为「凝光成形」「明镜止水」「浮光掠影」「幻镜移光」「镜里凝光」「世外春秋」。「凝光成形」在出征或合体镜汐时提升角色威能增幅、共鸣之力，并提升当前出征或合体所有幻兽的攻击力，释放「水镜破魔」结束后召唤镜沙共同作战；「明镜止水」在镜汐出征或合体时，提升角色及出征幻兽的最终伤害，技能升级至一定等级后，释放「水镜破魔」对命中目标施加眩晕与减速效果；「浮光掠影」在镜汐出征或合体时，提升角色及出征幻兽的神圣伤害；将技能升级至一定等级后，释放「水镜破魔」将赋予角色及出征幻兽移动速度加成；「幻镜移光」在镜汐出征或合体时，为受到攻击的角色提供护盾值，若攻击方为玩家则随机复制其一个防御增益，升级后获得护盾值的同时获得攻击方的一个防御增益效果「镜里凝光」根据镜汐养成进度对「水镜破魔」的固定伤害进行额外加成；「世外春秋」根据镜汐养成进度，在出征或合体镜汐时提升最终伤害。
4个专属非战技能分别为「踏水行波」「镜映彩池」「飞虹舞镜」「水镜裁影」。「踏水行波」为骑乘技能，可召唤坐骑「水镜麒麟」；「镜映彩池」为骑乘技能，可召唤坐骑「彩池浮镜」；「飞虹舞镜」为炫耀技能，使用后召唤镜汐一展舞姿，使宝镜之中重现彩池澜境；「水镜裁影」为击杀特效，装备后击杀目标时显示特殊光效。
助战玩法：指定全能幻兽符合对应档位条件时可直接提分并减免养成消耗
使用彩池浮光镜召唤「澜境君·镜汐」后即可开启助战。指定全能幻兽可参与助战。助战分为1至5档，各档位享受对应养成阶段的回响灵玉消耗减免。其中，第3、4、5档可分别将镜汐直接提升至1500、2000、2500分，第1、2档的官方表格未列直接提分数值。具体优惠阶段及次数按对应档位执行。持有6件法器的火莲战神、评分等于2000的嫦娥或神都女帝、2500至3000分的青霞、紫霞、昭君、渔歌、忘忧为镜汐助战后，其幻兽形象、坐骑形象仍将自动保留为魔法石；使用魔法石可解锁对应形象外观，并指定幻兽栏内的任意幻兽进行更换。
常见问题（FAQ）
1、镜汐在正式服和先锋区分别什么时候上线？
正式服于10月23日维护后上线，「聚灵返臻」持续至11月24日21:59；先锋区于10月21日维护后上线，「聚灵返臻」持续至11月22日21:59。
2、至臻榜单怎么参与，排名看什么？
镜汐达到3000分即可登记参与至臻榜单角逐，榜单根据镜汐被投喂的灵蕴数量进行排名，系统按排名发放光效、称号卡、外套包等奖励。
3、灵蕴有哪些获取方式？
1500分及以上的镜汐每24小时可产出一定数量灵蕴，评分越高产出越多；也可通过游戏内发布求购信息从其他勇士处获得；多余灵蕴可在「聚灵返臻」活动界面出售。
4、镜汐一共有哪些技能？
镜汐共有1个主动技能「水镜破魔」、6个被动技能「凝光成形」「明镜止水」「浮光掠影」「幻镜移光」「镜里凝光」「世外春秋」，以及4个专属非战技能「踏水行波」「镜映彩池」「飞虹舞镜」「水镜裁影」。
5、助战玩法怎么开启，有什么作用？
使用彩池浮光镜召唤镜汐后即可开启助战；指定全能幻兽参与助战后，符合对应档位条件时可直接提分，并在各养成阶段提供回响灵玉消耗减免。
6、助战幻兽的形象会保留吗？
持有6件法器的火莲战神、评分等于2000的嫦娥或神都女帝、2500至3000分的青霞、紫霞、昭君、渔歌、忘忧为镜汐助战后，其幻兽形象、坐骑形象仍将自动保留为魔法石；使用魔法石可解锁对应形象外观，并指定幻兽栏内的任意幻兽进行更换。

members.title: Rethinking the funnel: where mobile gaming really fits in the marketing mix

news.body:
Rethinking the funnel: where mobile gaming really fits in the marketing mix
We spoke with leaders across the digital advertising industry while at Cannes this year. Here's how they think about mobile gaming's role in the funnel, and why certain notions around gaming being purely performance and lower-funnel is being challenged.
A consumer’s path to conversion is no longer linear and is made up of moments to engage based on intent, context, and receptivity - and mobile gaming can play at each stage.
In this new pinball machine era of how brands can engage with consumers, mobile gaming seems to be able to capture consumers at different stages of intention. The attention quality inside a gaming environment, full screen, active engagement, an audience that's opted in to the experience, creates conditions that are well suited to direct response and brand building.
What makes mobile gaming genuinely distinctive is that the upper funnel argument and the lower funnel argument don't have to be in competition. The channel can support both, and increasingly, the infrastructure exists to prove it.
The storytelling opportunity reinforces this. Gaming environments offer something rare in digital advertising: extended, uninterrupted time with a consumer who is actively engaged with a screen. That has implications for brand recall and re-engagement that go well beyond what most performance-first strategies are designed to capture.
Non-endemic categories are beginning to take notice. Healthcare, a sector with some of the most stringent requirements around brand safety and audience targeting, offers a useful signal for how brands outside gaming's traditional advertiser base are starting to evaluate the channel.
For performance-focused buyers, the evolution of mobile gaming's role in the funnel is less about abandoning what the channel already does well and more about expanding how it's planned for.
What this means for programmatic teams: don't let legacy classification determine your strategy. Mobile gaming is a full-funnel channel, and the teams planning it that way are getting more out of it.
As mobile gaming continues to move further up the funnel, the conversation extends beyond planning to trust. Greater transparency into the advertising experience—through initiatives like Unity Core Standards—helps give marketers more confidence in where and how their brands appear, supporting the channel's continued evolution.
*We invited guests into our content studio to share their perspectives on the mobile gaming industry. The views expressed are their own.

10月17日至18日，《荒野乱斗》全球锦标赛最后一搏资格赛（Last Chance Qualifier，简称LCQ）在广州举行。经过两天的比赛，战队NAVI和Team Heretics成功突围，赢得通往全球总决赛的2张金票。
17日中午来到《荒野乱斗》LCQ的现场时，我有些惊讶，观众比我预想的多了太多。穿过一条几十米的长廊，我来到二楼活动区，从这里到一楼，到处都挤满了前来观赛的观众。周边售卖区排起长队，旁边圈出来的玩家对战区也已经人满为患。这一切都不太像我刻板印象中一款“小众游戏”该有的样子。
这并非我的第一次惊讶。接到《荒野乱斗》LCQ的邀请时，我就惊讶不已。此前我从未想过一款快节奏、轻量级的游戏能够举办全球性的电竞比赛，更没有想过其全球性赛事能够落地中国。相比海外，这里已经失去太多玩家基础。
说《荒野乱斗》是一款“小众游戏”也许并不完全合适。如果把时间往回拨6年，那时没有人会作出这样的判断。2020年6月《荒野乱斗》国服刚一上线，就火爆全网。首日即空降iOS畅销榜第4位，此后更是上升至榜单第2位，而榜单首位则是当时已经确立了国民手游地位的《王者荣耀》。
那年夏天对我来说同样难忘。6月大学毕业前的最后时刻，我们已经被封锁在校园中4个月之久。百无聊赖中，我和几位室友发现了当时火热的《荒野乱斗》。3分钟一场的快节奏对局，为我们带来了难得的新鲜和快乐。很快我们毕业了，四个人各奔东西，《荒野乱斗》也躺在手机里再也没有打开过。
后来，我很少再听到《荒野乱斗》的消息，直到这一次LCQ来到广州。《荒野乱斗》像是一位阔别多年的老朋友。往日荣光已经黯淡，从平凡处归来的他拿出一张张金票，邀请我们一起再向前去。
“金票”是《荒野乱斗》游戏中的一个概念，相当于现在各类网游中的付费系统——“战令”。本次LCQ决出全球总决赛的最后2个席位，通往这2个席位的资格被具象成了2张巨大的金票。然而2天的活动中，最先获得金票的却并非优胜的战队，而是完成现场活动的玩家。
本次LCQ的主办方别出心裁，将《荒野乱斗》中的各种游戏模式移植到线下。排队进入活动区，最先看到的是“乱斗篮球”。游戏中“乱斗篮球”模式的目标是抢夺场地上的篮球，投入对方的篮筐。活动现场将其改版成了限时竞速投篮。
再向场地内部深入，出现的是“幸运芭菲”。游戏中这是一台可以抓取技能增益扭蛋的抓娃娃机。现场几乎完美复刻了这款抓娃娃机的外观，只是没能复刻玩家每次出手必中的体验。
来到一楼，是开服版本的经典模式“宝石争霸”。游戏中需要收集10颗宝石。现场玩家则要从整整一个矿车的干扰项中，快速找到唯一的那颗宝石。
完成活动收集盖章后，玩家来到“金票之旅”区域，从整整一面墙的金票中挑选一张撕下。现场玩家小心翼翼地将自己金票收好，面带微笑地走入观赛区。
在现场，我见到的玩家大多符合这样的画像：衣着简单干净，面容稍显青涩。排队等候时少有人攀谈，多是在低头各自玩手机。队伍里这样的男生很多，女生则要我走上十几步才能见到一位。二十岁上下的男大学生构成观赛玩家的主体。
颇显矛盾的是，这群玩家又多是资深的老玩家。问起他们的游戏年限，他们告诉我，“五年”、“六年”。还有一位玩家克制着自己的激动，“我从国服开服就开始玩。不，从国际服就开始玩。”
对于一位二十多岁的玩家，六年已经占据了他们生命的四分之一。这段时间里，游戏热度下降，周围的朋友逐渐离开，“学校里一万人，找不到第二个（玩家）”。可他们仍然活跃在游戏里，仍然相聚在了LCQ的现场。
问及一直玩下来的原因，玩家们有些不善言辞。他们好像没有想过太多，只是脱口而出的一句热爱，将日复一日的坚守轻轻带过。
作为一个开服时短暂体验过《荒野乱斗》的回归玩家，我对其电竞比赛的期待不高。在我的印象里，这款游戏英雄机制简单、对局时间过短、双方博弈深度浅，很难构成一场高质量的比赛。这2天的比赛却完全是我预期的反面。
本次LCQ共有15场比赛，其中6场战至3:2，打满最后一局才宣告结束。打满的比赛占比四成，足以说明比赛的激烈程度。而现场的体验更是直观，每隔不到2分钟，观众席就要发出一阵惊叹、欢呼和掌声。
构成我观赛体验的首先是新鲜。
和很多战斗竞技类游戏不同，《荒野乱斗》没有主模式。十几个游戏目标完全不同的模式在游戏中定期轮换，供玩家自由选择。竞技性的排位赛，则更是每局都由系统随机选择一种模式。
本次LCQ的比赛中，每场比赛的5局游戏也是5个不同的模式。赛前双方轮流选择每个模式的地图。不同的游戏模式排序和不同的地图选择，使得的每场比赛的观赛体验都不尽相同。
比赛中的游戏模式可简单分为两类：一类以战斗减员为目标，一类不以战斗减员为目标。前者中，英雄死亡直接作为胜负指标，选手操作谨慎，现场的观赛范围十分紧张。后者中，英雄死亡并不直接影响胜负，选手打法积极，现场的观赛氛围也比较热烈。
5局游戏不同比赛模式随机排列，天然地赋予了整场比赛丰富多变的体验。即便每日都要战至深夜，观赛的新鲜感却从未消失。
我的第二重观赛体验是紧张。
《荒野乱斗》的游戏设计，为战斗双方提供了大量的翻盘机会。到了高水平的竞技赛场上，更是每一秒都有翻盘的可能，不到最后一秒没有什么能够尘埃落定。
小组赛SCKalalas对阵LOUD，第3局“赏金猎人”模式，游戏尾声，双方的“赏金之星”数量为5:5。比分相同的情况下，拥有蓝色“赏金之星”的LOUD获胜。
SCKalalas只有在计时结束前击杀一名敌方英雄，抢下其身上的“赏金之星”才能逆转。然而LOUD的防守始终滴水不漏。直到最后1秒，SCKalalas成功突破，完成关键击杀，游戏翻盘。
上半区半决赛Team Heretics对阵LOUD，第1局为“金库攻防”模式。该模式以攻击对方后场金库为比赛目标。率先攻破对方金库或计时结束时金库剩余生命值更高的队伍获胜。
这局比赛第1小局最后一秒时，Team Heretics金库剩余生命值30%落后于LOUD的36%。然而就在这一秒钟内，Team Heretics冲向对方金库，将其剩余生命值打至29%，以1%的优势拿下这一小局。
2天比赛下来，我已经数不清类似的场面发生了多少次。在这里，没有前期运营锁定胜局，只有最后一秒一绝胜负。
最后，我的观赛体验被感动定格。
本次LCQ共有2支来自中国的战队TOC和Ace Xero入围。遗憾的是，比赛首日，2只队伍便在小组赛中出局。赛后围绕他们，更多的不是批评和质疑，而是赞赏和鼓励。
相比另外6支战队，这2支中国战队十分特殊。他们没有加入俱乐部，更没有资本化运营。有观众将他们称作“就是四个热爱游戏的大学生”。还有观众评价说，“他们的表现已经很不错了，那场打SKC不是还差点‘让二追三’。”
我在现场看到的，是一群热爱者闯进全球赛事的故事。观众席上，另一群热爱者激动地为中国战队举起应援牌，是因为他们的亮眼表现，也是因为热爱无关胜负。
除了2支中国战队，还有一位选手触动了全场观众的内心。KDS战队的Bobby曾5次入围全球赛事，并在2023年获得全球总决赛亚军。今年26岁的他向职业生涯的最后一次全球总决赛发起冲刺。2天的比赛中，Bobby多次打出精彩操作。下半区半决赛对阵LOUD，他的皮尔斯在关键对局中连续走位，残血躲掉对面4个技能，成为整场LCQ最高光的时刻之一。
本次LCQ的最后一场比赛，KDS和Team Heretics争夺最后一个全球总决赛的席位。KDS连丢2局的情况下，Bobby在第三局选出了他的成名的英雄——佩佩。现场解说激动地称之为“很可能是最后一舞”。尽管Bobby的佩佩狙击精准、操作亮眼，KDS还是憾负第3局，0:3止步广州。比赛结束，现场观众齐声高喊Bobby的名字送别这位昔日王者。此刻，比赛的胜负都让位于情怀与热爱。这份感动成为了本次LCQ我最美妙的记忆。
18日比赛落幕时，NAVI和Team Heretics赢下了LCQ的两张金票，开启从广州去往东京全球总决赛的旅程。
赛后，玩家们拿出自己的那张金票，再次排起长队，等待喜爱的选手签名。离开赛场时，天色彻底暗了下来，有玩家再次举起那张金票，借着朋友手机上的闪光灯，留下和赛场的最后一张合影。
这张金票明天就要再次出发。

news.summary_raw: Side宣布收购成都精品游戏美术工作室Roboto Entertainment，创始人Andrea Cordella出任Side全球美术总监并负责成都新工作室，强化全球美术服务能力，扩大在华业务布局。

members.title: Side收购精品游戏美术工作室Roboto Entertainment，进一步扩展创意服务

news.body:
Side在成都成立新工作室，Roboto Entertainment创始人Andrea Cordella将被任命为Side全球美术总监
10月22日于中国成都——行业领先的全球游戏服务提供商Side于今日宣布，正式收购精品游戏美术工作室Roboto Entertainment，进一步强化其全球美术服务能力，并扩大在中国大陆的业务布局。Roboto Entertainment创始人Andrea Cordella将出任Side全球美术总监，领导Side的全球美术部门，并担任成都新工作室的负责人。他带领的团队将与Side上海团队及遍布美洲、中东、欧洲、非洲和亚洲的美术及联合开发团队紧密合作。
“今年科隆游戏展的开幕之夜直播中，有半数作品来自中国，这让全世界的目光都投向了这里。长期以来，中国一直是游戏行业最重要的市场之一，我们在中国的团队期待参与更多项目，我为此感到无比自豪。因此，我们决定进一步扩大在中国的业务规模。”Side首席执行官Deborah Kirkham表示。
尽管全球游戏行业近几年的增长有所放缓，中国市场预计仍将在2026年增长4%，并于2030年达到598亿美元的市场规模。中国的玩家活跃度、电竞参与度、游戏时长和游戏消费均位居世界前列，使其成为对全球游戏开发商极具吸引力的市场。
“本次收购是我们进一步深化区域战略布局的重要举措。随着Andrea出任全球美术总监，以及成都新工作室的成立，我们将汇聚业内顶尖的环境美术与游戏世界构建人才。”Kirkham补充道。
Andrea Cordella于2014年创立了Roboto Entertainment，专注于游戏环境美术和世界构建。这支总部位于成都的团队曾参与开发多款3A和2A级别的游戏，涵盖主机端和移动平台。
Andrea Cordella表示：“从初次接触到Deborah和Side团队的那一刻起，我就知道这家公司与我和我的团队所珍视的价值观高度契合。我们追求卓越，并将创意铭记于心——游戏是唯一一种消费者与创作者扮演同等角色的艺术媒介。我们将继续把创意融入每一个项目中，与全球团队开展合作，为开发者不同类型的项目提供支持。我已经迫不及待要开启这段新的旅程了。”
Side在今年的科隆游戏展上，还宣布了与行业领先的AI游戏测试平台Modl.ai建立合作伙伴关系，进一步拓展了游戏测试服务。Side提供的服务涵盖玩家客服、游戏测试、本地化、本地化测试、数据集、联合开发、美术和音频服务，目前已经在为中国的开发者提供全方位支持。
成都工作室的成立，加上Andrea Cordella及其团队在环境美术领域的专业实力，将进一步提升Side的服务能力，为中国及全球其他市场的开发者提供更全面的支持。
关于Side：
Side是全球领先的游戏开发与服务提供商，为许多世界知名的开发商和工作室提供技术与创意解决方案。Side成立于2009年，起源于日本，如今已成长为立足于科技行业的全球企业，并在全球12个国家拥有超过15间工作室，足迹遍布美洲、欧洲、以及亚洲。其行业领先的服务涵盖美术制作、游戏开发、游戏测试、玩家客服、社群管理、本地化、本地化测试、音频制作以及数据集。欲了解更多信息，请访问www.side.inc

news.title: Tomb Raider Director Explains How 3D Level Design Has Evolved Over 30 Years
news.summary_raw: Tomb Raider Game Director Raul Siqueira discusses 30 years of 3D level design, preserving isolation, evolving camera technology, and Legacy of Atlantis’ optional guidance systems.

members.title: Tomb Raider Director Explains How 3D Level Design Has Evolved Over 30 Years

news.body:
Tomb Raider Director Explains How 3D Level Design Has Evolved Over 30 Years
Tomb Raider Game Director Raul Siqueira discusses 30 years of 3D level design, preserving isolation, evolving camera technology, and Legacy of Atlantis’ optional guidance systems.
In case you missed it
30 Years of Tomb Raider
When the original Tomb Raider arrived in 1996, fully three-dimensional action-adventure games were still establishing their fundamental rules. Its environments were not simply backdrops or corridors connecting encounters. Players had to study their surroundings, understand how spaces connected, judge distances, and identify routes through architecture that initially appeared impassable. That was over 30 years ago.
Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is reimagining Lara’s first adventure for modern hardware, creating an unusual design challenge: how do you preserve the satisfaction of independently reading an environment while remaining approachable to players raised on objective markers, highlighted routes, and contextual hints? The developers’ answer is to let players decide how much assistance they receive.
We spoke with Crystal Dynamics Game Director Raul Siqueira about Tomb Raider’s contribution to 3D exploration, how camera technology changed the construction of environments and challenges, and why preserving the original game’s sense of isolation remains so important. Siqueira also discussed designing for several generations of players and using optional assistance to remove barriers without removing the thrill of discovery.
Legacy of Atlantis is being developed by Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog and will launch on February 12, 2027, for PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2.
The original Tomb Raider arrived when fully 3D environments were still relatively new. What did the game establish about movement, navigation, and spatial reasoning that influenced the wider industry?
Raul Siqueira, Game Director: I think the original Tomb Raider was a pioneer for what we currently know as a 3D action-adventure game. Some concepts from it obviously went through iteration as time went by; things like controls and combat have primarily changed a lot, however the core of exploration and navigation still holds up to this day.
Is anyone from that original team working on the newer games?
Raul Siqueira: We have a surprising number of people who have been working on this franchise for over 20 years, but unfortunately no one from the original six devs from the very first game.
Early Tomb Raider levels were often built around interconnected spaces that players had to observe and gradually understand. Why was learning the architecture itself such an important part of the experience?
Raul Siqueira: It speaks to the cerebral nature of the original game, asking players to slow down and pay attention to their surroundings as a way of finding the path forward. It helps put players in the shoes of an explorer; it serves the fantasy of playing as someone like Lara Croft.
Tomb Raider has traditionally provided relatively little direct guidance, asking players to identify routes through landmarks, lighting, geometry, and environmental clues. How has the series’ approach to spatial readability evolved as player expectations have changed?
Raul Siqueira: Different eras of Tomb Raider have carried different philosophies, largely reflecting what was expected from games of that genre at the time. But if you look at the arc of the series, you can see a clear evolution, from offering very little guidance in the early days, to guiding players more in later entries, to where we are now: giving players the ability to decide for themselves how much guidance they want.
The Tomb Raider franchise is celebrating its 30-year milestone this month, and that means our audience spans an incredibly wide range of gaming backgrounds. Some players grew up navigating the original games with nothing but their instincts, and others discovered the series through the Survivor trilogy and its more modern conventions. They're all looking for something different, and we want to honor that.
In Legacy of Atlantis, players can independently adjust settings across combat, puzzle hints, and exploration guidance, so you're never locked into a single, rigid difficulty tier. Want brutal encounters but gentle nudges on puzzles? That's your call. The goal is to remove barriers without removing the thrill of discovery.
Cameras have changed significantly across Tomb Raider’s history, from fixed or tightly controlled perspectives to modern third-person systems. How has camera technology influenced the kinds of environments, jumps, puzzles, and dramatic reveals the designers can create?
Raul Siqueira: The camera is an important part of any action-adventure game. Framing puzzle elements or the destination of a tricky jump can be what makes or breaks a specific challenge. So often in the past, layouts had to go through heavy iteration to circumvent camera limitations. Luckily, modern technology has made it possible for designers to quickly author different camera behaviors and create more interesting challenges because of it.
Modern players are accustomed to objective markers, highlighted ledges, survival vision, and other navigational assistance. How do you preserve the satisfaction of discovering a path while ensuring players understand the visual language of a level?
Raul Siqueira: It all comes down to player agency. For Legacy of Atlantis, we offer several options that allow players to tune the experience to their liking. If you want the old-school experience of working through challenges until you figure them out on your own, that option is absolutely there. But if you'd prefer a helping hand, you can turn on hints and guidance tools. For example, Lara can provide voice clues for puzzles, and she has a scanner that helps guide players along the way. Crucially though, you have the ability to turn off the voice cues for puzzles and choose not to use the scanner if you feel they detract from the exploration experience.
Beyond that, it really comes down to the UI and UX side of things, and how we communicate information so that players know exactly what they're signing up for before they begin. We think carefully about how our tutorials are presented, how text is displayed, and whether it all makes intuitive sense. When you pick up the scanner for the first time, for instance, we present clear screenshots, so players understand every nuance and option at their disposal. The way we present and communicate these tools is one of the key ways we balance these philosophies for all types of players. We can't do it for everything, but we focus on how much of it is important to surface before players even start their journey. That was a major focus during development: making sure we had a strong solution from a UI and UX perspective so that when a player boots up the game for the first time, they understand what those options offer and can feel satisfied with the gameplay experience they've customized for themselves.
Once you're in the game, we also rely on a visual language that moves away from traditional markers. Over the past couple of years, we've seen a lot of feedback pushing back against games that signpost where to go next too overtly or trigger voice cues too quickly. So how do you strike the right balance? For us, the answer is visual design. We want players to be able to read the environment and intuit where to go through the level design itself, without the game explicitly telling them.
Looking across 30 years of Tomb Raider, which aspects of its original level-design philosophy remain essential to the series, regardless of changes in technology and audience expectations?
Raul Siqueira: The original level design did a phenomenal job at giving players a sense of isolation, and that is something we very much wanted to preserve in Legacy of Atlantis.
What do you hope a new generation of developers takes from Tomb Raider’s contribution to 3D exploration and level design?
Raul Siqueira: My hope is that we have players who are now playing the Tomb Raider games that are coming out and will be the next generation of Tomb Raider developers, so we can continue something that is very special to the franchise, which is not just to have great game developers working on the games, but to have great developers that are also Tomb Raider fans.

news.title: Substance 3D Painter 12.2 Lets Artists Paint Baking Cages Directly on Models
news.summary_raw: Substance 3D Painter 12.2 introduces cage painting, smarter Polygon Fill selections, texture-set highlighting, and improved real-time rendering for overlapping transparent materials.

members.title: Substance 3D Painter 12.2 Lets Artists Paint Baking Cages Directly on Models

news.body:
Substance 3D Painter 12.2 Lets Artists Paint Baking Cages Directly on Models
Substance 3D Painter 12.2 introduces cage painting, smarter Polygon Fill selections, texture-set highlighting, and improved real-time rendering for overlapping transparent materials.
In case you missed it
Substance 3D Painter Interview
Adobe has released Substance 3D Painter 12.2, introducing several workflow improvements intended to reduce the repetitive setup, selection, and troubleshooting involved in texturing detailed 3D assets.
The update’s biggest addition is cage painting, which gives artists more direct control over projection distances during baking. Painter uses a cage to determine how far it should search beyond a low-poly mesh when capturing detail from its high-resolution counterpart. A cage that is too close can miss details, while one that extends too far can capture information from unintended surfaces.
Artists can now paint the cage distance directly onto their model with per-pixel brush control or use Polygon Fill to adjust complete sub-objects. This should make it easier to identify and correct local projection problems before committing to another bake instead of repeatedly changing the entire cage and checking the result.
Cage Painting
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 Features
The feature continues Adobe’s recent effort to make Painter’s baking workflow more interactive. Version 12.1 introduced automatic rebaking and the ability to paint skew corrections directly onto low-poly geometry. Cage painting now applies a similar visual workflow to another common source of baking artifacts.
Polygon Fill has also received three selection modes. Rectangular Marquee allows artists to drag across a chosen area, Polygon Loop selects a continuous loop of faces, and Partial Polygon Loop targets a smaller portion when a complete loop would include too much geometry.
A new Visible Polygons Only option prevents rectangular selections from passing through the model and affecting polygons on its opposite side. This seemingly small addition addresses a persistent frustration when masking geometry in the 3D viewport, particularly on dense meshes or assets containing overlapping parts.
Polygon Fill
Texture Set Highlighter
Painter 12.2 also introduces Texture Set Highlighting. Hovering over a texture set illuminates its corresponding geometry in the viewport, while holding Ctrl/Cmd + Alt and hovering over the model identifies which set contains that part. The feature should be especially helpful when opening unfamiliar projects or navigating characters and props divided across numerous materials.
Finally, Order Independent Transparency improves the viewport rendering of glass, ice, liquids, and other low-opacity materials. When several transparent surfaces overlap, Painter can now sort them more accurately, producing a clearer real-time preview of their intended appearance.
Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is available now. Adobe’s full technical breakdown and list of fixes can be found in the official release notes. Readers can also revisit 80 Level’s interview on Substance 3D Painter’s role in modern production pipelines and the additions introduced with version 12.0.

news.summary_raw: Steam's October 2026 Next Fest edition features over 8,000 game demos, which is two times more than what we saw in June.

members.title: What to Play During Steam's Next Fest 2026: Best Games to Try

news.body:
What to Play During Steam's Next Fest 2026: Best Games to Try
Steam's October 2026 Next Fest edition features over 8,000 game demos, which is two times more than what we saw in June.
The October chapter of Steam's Next Fest 2026 brought us over 8,000 game demos to check out. While many of them are infamously fully made with AI, there are some true gems on the list.
We've compiled our favorites across different genres, styles, and game types. You might recognize some of the titles from our previous articles and developer interviews. Let us know in the comments which ones you've tested out and enjoyed.
Loftia
Loftia is a cute multiplayer game where you build a whole new world in the sky. It's a relaxing yet beautifully executed lesson on eco-consciousness: while crafting your cozy corner, you will learn to use renewable energy sources and master sustainable farming techniques. You will build community by befriending the NPCs and helping them out by accepting various quests. Plus, of course, you will meet adorable animals you can take care of and adopt, and they, in turn, will accompany you on this journey.
Qloud Games
Hela: Of Mice & Magic
Continuing the topic of nature-inspired cozy adventures, we have the endlessly adorable story about mice who take matters into their own little paws to protect their forest, once guarded by a witch who fell ill. In Hela: Of Mice & Magic, you will collect ingredients, brew magical potions, solve environmental puzzles, and help your forest community by completing exciting missions. The breathtaking locations you explore in the game are inspired by the landscapes of Northern Sweden.
Windup
Reshine
If you like to look for beauty in details and enjoy hand-crafted pieces with history, you'll love this relaxing cleaning simulator. In Reshine, you have to take care of vintage objects that have gone through a lot and need some love, cleaning, and polishing. In a quiet, cozy attic full of instruments, you will take old pieces apart, clean them with different tools to remove dust and chipped paint, repair them if needed, reassemble all the details, and apply a shiny, fresh coating to make them look as good as new.
Quite OK Games
Haunted Paws
We've been eyeing this cozy horror co-op for a while now. In Haunted Paws, you play as two puppies who are on a mission to rescue their owner from a haunted mansion. Together with your friend, you will explore dark environments full of secrets, defeat scary creatures to set them free, and solve puzzles. You can pick your favorite dog breed to play as and customize the puppies to fight evil spirits while staying fresh and cute.
LazyFlock
UNFROST
This co-op survival horror set in Antarctica is an intense, atmospheric shooter where you fight enormous Lovecraftian creatures. In UNFROST, not only do you have to survive extreme conditions in this frozen land, but you also need to study the behavior of the Riftborne, the mysterious giant monsters, to attack them efficiently and make sure they don't get you first. You also need to monitor weather conditions, because when brutal blizzards take over, your chances of survival are next to none. Read our interview with the developers to discover how they built the world of UNFROST.
Nord Unit
Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy
Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy is a cinematic, story-rich survival horror game full of mystery. In the third chapter of the dark story of Remothered, the main character's daughter has been kidnapped, and now you have to do everything in your power to save her. For those who love all things supernatural, this game is a gem: you'll have to use retrocognition, mirror abilities, and moth manipulation to access what's beneath the surface and warp the environment to find hidden paths and clues.
Stormind Games
Inkblood
Inkblood is not quite what you expect from a point-and-click detective game. In this occult puzzle, you take on the role of an investigator traveling the gloomy land filled with dark secrets in a carriage. You observe everything around you from the carriage window, and a special tool helps you uncover more than you'd expect. A magnifying glass that reveals events of the past will help you compare what you see to what happened before or, better yet, catch someone trying to conceal their deeds. Read our interview with Inkblood's developers to find out how they built this intricate visual puzzle.
HeyBird!
Demi and the Fractured Dream
In this stunning action-adventure reminiscent of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, you play as Demi, a Voidsent creature. The curse of the void can both weaken you and help you unleash great powers. On your journey through the world of Somnus, you will have to defeat the Accursed Beasts to save the world. As you travel through the deep dungeons in Demi and the Fractured Dream, you will solve puzzles and use a whole arsenal of attacks, spells, and tools to fight ferocious monsters.
Yarn Owl Studios
Alchemortis
It would be impossible to complete this list without a retro-style pixel-art game, and Alchemortis is a perfect one to fill this spot. It's an absurdly stylish roguelike inventory management auto-battler. Like a true evil alchemist, you will transmute and combine items to merge their stats, properties, and forms. If you organize them wisely in your inventory, you'll unlock powerful effects and create killer combinations. You will also discover new characters who will, in turn, give you access to entirely new playstyles.
Firebelley
Guns of Eschaton
This soulslike FPS with Dune-style environments and giant creatures is an emotionally charged apocalyptic Western from Viktor Antonov, the art director behind Half-Life 2, Fallout 4, and Dishonored. Guns of Eschaton became Antonov last title, as he passed away in February 2025.
The environments in the game are mind-blowing, the monsters you need to fight on your way through this hell are unbelievable, and the combat mechanics are surprisingly tricky to master. Unlike your usual shooter, where grabbing a heavier gun and blasting bigger bullets is enough to carry you through the game, here, it's not enough. You need to study the weaknesses of each creature you encounter and the specifications of each weapon to carry out precise, intentional attacks.
Eschatology Entertainment
While these are our picks from Steam's Next Fest, there are, of course, a lot more games that deserve your attention. Let us know which you tried and which would make it to your personal top-10.

news.title: AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling is coming to Xbox Series X|S
news.summary_raw: Microsoft and AMD have announced that AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling technology is coming to Xbox Series X|S consoles.

members.title: AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling is coming to Xbox Series X|S

news.body:
AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling is coming to Xbox Series X|S
Microsoft and AMD have announced the machine-learning tech for current Xbox consoles, but have not given a release date.
Microsoft and AMD have announced that AMD's FSR 4.1 upscaling technology is coming to Xbox Series X|S consoles.
While there's no release date beyond "soon," Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet confirmed the plan in an announcement video.
According to GameSpot, Van Vliet said AMD has been a partner for more than two decades, and that Microsoft and AMD are also working together on Project Helix, the next-generation Xbox.
FSR 4.1 is a machine-learning-based temporal upscaler, which renders a game at a lower resolution and reconstructs it at a higher one.
It will also support Radeon RX 6000-series graphics cards, Gorgon Halo and Strix Halo Ryzen 9 laptops, and handhelds such as the Asus ROG Xbox Ally devices, which use Z2 Extreme and Z2A chips.
AMD did not share any other details for Xbox Series X|S. Developers will have to patch their games to use FSR 4.1, so older titles won't upgrade automatically.
Series X|S also lack dedicated machine-learning hardware, so gains are unlikely to match the PS5 Pro, where Sony already offers its own upscalers, PSSR and QSSR.
Earlier today, we reported that Project Helix is reportedly launching in the 2028 holiday season and is projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800. Deadlines have reportedly been moved up "by at least several months" on Helix, "putting pressure on development teams to get the work done faster, including using AI."
CEO Asha Sharma said that Xbox won't use "AI for AI's sake" and that it would be used as a tool for engineering and performance issues.
We also learned that Xbox's restructuring is ongoing, with additional layoffs expected this month, in November, and January.

news.title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 4, Setting (and hitting) quarterly rocks
news.summary_raw: Previously in this series, we've defined your studio purpose , set clear goals for the future , and looked at how to catch and solve the problems that get in the way . This week, we're tackling one of the crucial tools for managing the work that needs to happen to hit your goals.

members.title: How to run an indie game studio: Part 4, Setting (and hitting) quarterly rocks

news.body:
How to run an indie game studio: Part 4, Setting (and hitting) quarterly rocks
Business coach Martijn van Zwieten on setting quarterly goals – rocks – that will keep your studio on course for its long-term aims
Previously in this series, we've defined your studio purpose, set clear goals for the future, and looked at how to catch and solve the problems that get in the way. This week, we're tackling one of the crucial tools for managing the work that needs to happen to hit your goals.
Why aren't yearly goals enough? Because a year is a long time. Long enough that it's easy to look up in October and realise you've been busy all year without meaningfully moving the needle on the things that actually matter. At the same time, a typical sprint is too short a horizon to make progress on anything substantial. You're more likely to prioritise the immediate and bump the important stuff that is harder to catch in a series of Jira tickets. Without something to focus your efforts in the middle distance, then, it's incredibly hard to make a series of short-term sprints build up to your yearly goals.
This is where quarterly rocks come in.
What are rocks?
The term "rocks" comes from a classic time management metaphor, introduced by Stephen Covey in The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. He relates a story where a professor displays an empty jar, and next to it are a pile of rocks, a pile of gravel, a pile of sand, and a pitcher of water. The cylinder represents your day, the rocks your main priorities, the gravel your day-to-day responsibilities, and the sand represents interruptions. The water is everything else that happens to us on a given day.
On any given day, most people tend to pour in the water first, then the sand, then the gravel, and quickly find out that, sadly, there's no more room for the rocks. Covey argues that if we prioritize the rocks and put them in the jar, followed by the gravel, the sand and the water, everything settles into the jar much easier. And even if some of the sand or water ends up not fitting, at least the things that truly mattered were taken care of.
In studio management, rocks are your quarterly goals – the four or five most important things your studio needs to achieve in the next 90 days.
Why 90 days?
A quarter is long enough to make real progress on something meaningful, and short enough that the end of it never feels too far away. When accountability is a year out, it's easy to get off track and deprioritise; when it's 90 days out, it's easier to stay focused.
It makes you chunk your yearly goals into concrete, near-term objectives
The quarterly rhythm also forces a discipline that annual planning alone cannot: it makes you chunk your yearly goals into concrete, near-term objectives. Saying you want to ship a vertical slice by the end of the year is a yearly goal. Asking "what needs to be true by the end of this quarter for us to be on track for that?" is how it becomes a rock. And because rocks are set as a team, they do something else that's crucial: they create alignment.
When everyone in your core team is involved in translating your yearly goals to quarterly priorities, making the high-level decisions that that requires, you're no longer pulling in subtly different directions based on different assumptions about what matters most right now. This typically prevents huge amounts of miscommunication, friction, and frustration down the line, which would otherwise translate to wasted time, effort, and money.
Setting your rocks
The rock-setting process is incredibly straightforward. With your yearly goals as the backdrop, sit down with your team and work through the question: what are the most important things we need to achieve in the next 90 days?
Get everyone's input on the table first, then cut the list down. The target is five to seven rocks – the same sweet spot as your yearly goals, for the same reason. Too many, and you'll be spread too thin to actually finish the things you started. Too few, and you're leaving results on the table. Five to seven forces genuine prioritisation, which forces you to have the often uncomfortable but crucial conversations about what actually matters most right now.
Each rock should be concrete enough that at the end of the quarter, you can look at it and say clearly: did we hit this or not? Vague rocks like "Make progress on the combat system" evade accountability, because they can always be called partially done. "Complete the core combat loop and have it playtested with ten players" cannot.
Once your rocks are set, everyone knows exactly what the studio is working towards. When new tasks surface, new opportunities arise, or someone wants to pull the team in a new direction, the question is always the same: does this serve our rocks? If yes, great. If not, it either waits or it doesn't happen. And in the edge case where something critical needs to take priority over your rocks, it's much easier to sit down and discuss which of the rocks needs to be dropped to make room for the new workload.
Built-in accountability
The final perk of working with rocks is that both reflection and accountability are baked into the design. At the end of every 90 days, you review and discuss your rocks together as a team. What did you hit? What did you miss? What got in the way?
The goal here is never to assign blame; the point is that you either win as a team or you learn as a team. A studio that honestly reviews its quarterly performance can learn from its failures and improve faster than one that just sets new goals without looking back. Over time, the quarterly review also gives you a much clearer picture of your studio's actual capacity, which makes future goal-setting more grounded and more realistic.
Applied consistently, rocks are a powerful tool for baking focus, alignment, and accountability into the fabric of your studio, speeding up your progress and the quality of your teamwork at the same time.
This week's homework
Together with your team, work through the following:
- Set your rocks for the next quarter. With your yearly goals in front of you, ask: what are the five to seven most important things we need to achieve in the next 90 days? Make sure each rock is specific enough that at the end of the quarter you'll be able to tell whether you hit it or not.
- Put the review in the calendar. Get into the habit of quarterly review and planning sessions by planning the next one right as you're starting the new quarter.
- Collect your purpose, BHAG, yearly goals and rocks in one central, convenient place. You've gone to the trouble of defining your purpose, BHAG, yearly goals and rocks, and we don't want these to go to waste. Collect them in a central place that's easy to access, so that people can actually use them as guidelines.
Next week, we wrap up the FIRM framework with the final pillar, and look at a format for your weekly, quarterly, and yearly meetings that will actually make you look forward to them.
Want the full FIRM framework with step-by-step implementation instructions? Visit martijnvanzwieten.com/firm to download the free template.
Martijn van Zwieten is a business and leadership coach, and the creator of the FIRM and LoGOS studio management methods. He has coached over 150 CEOs, founders, and leaders to build better studios, ranging from indie darlings like Rusty Lake and Twirlbound to AAA powerhouses like Bethesda Game Studios and MachineGames.

members.title: Project Helix reportedly launching in late 2028, projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800

news.body:
Project Helix reportedly launching in late 2028, projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800
Fortune reports that Xbox is also planning to launch a next-gen handheld device next year
Project Helix is reportedly launching in the 2028 holiday season and is projected to cost between $1,200 and $1,800.
Fortune recently spoke with Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and other sources familiar with Xbox and Microsoft, with the latter providing details on the current pipeline for Xbox's next-generation console.
According to these sources, deadlines have been moved up "by at least several months" on Helix, "putting pressure on development teams to get the work done faster, including using AI.
Sharma told Fortune that Xbox won't use "AI for AI's sake," and that it would be used as a tool for engineering and performance issues.
She previously said that Xbox is prioritising "efficiency and affordability alongside performance" for its next-generation console. "All of us need to be thinking about and innovating on and giving people more choice in terms of how they play their console and how they purchase their console."
Xbox is also reportedly planning to launch a next-gen handheld device by late next year.
Xbox is also reportedly planning a Game Pass overhaul, which may allow players to select "add-ons for console-only games, cloud gaming, and multiplayer, with the system operating on a tiered structure."
As of July 2026, Xbox Game Pass subscribers totaled less than 50% of the original target. Sharma previously said the company had "bet on Game Pass" as well as "multi-platform and a broader portfolio of content."
"While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in history. We must reset Xbox."
Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty also told Fortune: "If there's any place that we got out of sync maybe in the last five years, it's not that any one of those [individual bets] wasn't working. It's just that we hadn't connected the dots maybe as well as we should have."
Xbox’s restructuring is ongoing, with Fortune reporting that Sharma is planning additional layoffs for this month, November, and January.
"Some employees have appreciated Sharma's transparency," the publication wrote, "but the decision to structure layoffs in several waves has left some staff demoralised, feeling as if they are sitting under a yearlong cloud, waiting to see if their roles are eliminated next."
Rumours of Xbox being prepared for an "eventual sale, spinoff, outside investment, or conversion into a subsidiary" were also highlighted.
Microsoft commercial business CEO Judson Althoff told Fortune that "Asha is one of the best leaders we have at the whole company. We would not have put her on a business we intend to sell. There's going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell."
As for Sharma's comment on the situation: "I think we're going to be an important part of Microsoft for a very long time."

members.title: 让恐龙狩猎不止于射击：专访《Turok: Origins》开发团队

features.body:
《Turok: Origins》是由 Saber Interactive 开发并发行的动作射击游戏，也是经典恐龙狩猎游戏系列《Turok》的全新作品。游戏将玩家带入一个融合了原始生态与科幻元素的世界：玩家将扮演 Turok 战士，穿梭于多个星球，在探索古老遗迹与陌生环境的过程中，与凶猛的恐龙及威胁人类生存的外星势力展开战斗。
在玩法上，本作保留了系列以武器战斗为核心的特点，同时加入了近战攻击、特殊能力与角色成长系统。玩家可以从倒下的敌人和环境中获取 DNA，解锁新的能力，并逐步强化战衣与自身的战斗能力。游戏还支持单人游玩和最多三人参与的合作模式，让玩家能够独自展开冒险，或是与队友共同面对失落之地的危险。
在 TGS2026 现场试玩《Turok: Origins》时，恐龙给我留下的印象并不只是它们的体型与外观。不同种类的敌人拥有各自的行动方式和攻击习惯，有些生物只有在玩家靠近后才会发起攻击，有些则会主动袭击玩家，甚至像捕食猎物一样追踪 Turok 战士。
在试玩结束后，机核有幸采访了《Turok: Origins》的开发团队，围绕恐龙敌人的设计思路、DNA 系统的作用、双视角的战斗设计，以及单人和合作模式之间的差异等话题展开了交流。
Q1. 在试玩过程中，我注意到《Turok: Origins》并不是简单地把恐龙当作普通敌人，而是利用它们不同的体型、行动方式和攻击模式来制造战斗变化。团队在设计恐龙敌人时，既需要考虑它们的生物特征，也需要赋予它们鲜明的战斗个性。你们是如何平衡这两个方面的？
A：这两个方面都非常重要。首先，设计团队会根据不同生态区域的需求，确定玩家将会遭遇哪些野生生物。在探索失落之地的不同星球时，玩家会遇到各具特色的本土生物，而它们的行为也存在明显差异。有些生物只有在玩家靠近时才会作出反应，有些则会一见到玩家就发动攻击，还有一些会将 Turok 士兵视作猎物，主动跟踪并展开捕猎。
在此基础上，概念设计、3D 制作和动画团队会参考现实中的生物资料，尽可能让这些生物的外观与行为显得真实、自然，同时又保留游戏本身的科幻气质。我们希望玩家面对不同敌人时，能够感受到它们在行为和战斗方式上的区别，而不只是看到外观有所不同的敌人。
Q2. 本作的 DNA 系统很有特色。玩家可以从敌人和环境中获取 DNA，并借此解锁新的能力，而这些能力的变化也会直接反映在 Turok 的战衣外观上。这套系统最初是如何构思出来的？在设计时，你们更希望它成为一种角色成长机制，还是希望它能够真正改变玩家应对战斗的方式？
A：从游戏构思之初，我们就认为 Turok 组织与周围环境之间的关系是密不可分的。因此，DNA 操控并不是一个孤立的玩法系统，而是贯穿整个游戏的核心概念。它既是游戏剧情的重要组成部分，也与 Turok 组织的设定、Xenia 的战斗风格，以及游戏的成长与进度系统密切相关。
这一理念也延伸到了游戏的各个部分。无论是 EchoSyncs 系统，还是其他成长机制与视觉表现，我们都希望它们能够体现 DNA 这一核心概念，让世界观与实际玩法形成联系。
正如你所提到的，我们也希望借助这套系统，为玩家提供更多战斗上的选择。不同玩家可以根据自己的喜好，决定如何运用所获得的能力，并以适合自己的方式应对战斗。通过这种设计，我们希望在丰富玩法的同时，为玩家带来更多样化的战斗体验。
Q3. 过去的《Turok》系列给玩家留下了比较深刻的第一人称射击印象，而《Turok: Origins》这次加入了第三人称视角。第三人称能够让玩家更直观地观察角色动作、武器和 DNA 能力带来的外观变化，但也意味着射击与近战的操作体验需要作出调整。团队是如何处理这次视角变化的？
A：第一人称视角对于延续系列的传统非常重要，它能够带来更强的沉浸感，以及更直接、激烈的战斗体验。与此同时，我们也希望通过加入第三人称视角，让游戏能够更好地适应现代玩家的习惯，并在平台跳跃与场景探索等环节中提供更直观的空间判断方式。
因此，我们允许玩家在两种视角之间无缝切换，让他们可以根据当前的游戏情境与个人偏好，自由选择合适的视角。
当然，两种视角并不是简单地共享同一套操作与动画。实际上，它们分别拥有独立的制作流程。例如，在第三人称视角下，玩家闪避时会做出翻滚动作；而在第一人称视角下，同样的操作则表现为一次快速冲刺。瞄准系统也会根据视角分别调整，包括视野范围和瞄准界面等细节。
我们还为所有武器制作了对应的 3D 模型与动画，确保它们能够在两种视角之间自然切换。至于一些重要能力和终结动作，则会以第三人称视角呈现，让玩家能够完整地看到角色的战衣与动作表现。这些细节都需要针对不同视角分别进行设计，才能确保两种模式都能提供合适的体验。
Q4. 本作既支持单人游玩，也支持多人合作。对于一款以狩猎恐龙为核心体验的游戏来说，合作模式显然能够带来更多战术配合的可能性。那么，单人模式与多人合作模式在实际体验上会有哪些区别？如果玩家选择独自游玩，是否也能体验到合作模式中的全部剧情与游戏内容？
A：无论选择单人游玩还是多人合作，玩家都能够体验相同的剧情战役、支线任务，以及可以反复挑战的任务内容。两种模式在可游玩的内容方面是一致的。
它们的主要区别在于任务的强度与难度。在单人模式下，玩家可以按照自己的节奏推进游戏，既可以积极投入战斗，也可以放慢脚步探索关卡，寻找隐藏路线与额外奖励。
而在合作模式中，随着队伍人数的变化，游戏的战斗节奏也会相应调整。敌人的数量会增加，攻击性也会进一步提升，从而让战斗变得更加紧张、激烈。
合作玩法的乐趣，则在于不同队员之间的配合。玩家可以围绕不同职业、武器和 EchoSyncs 能力展开协作，尝试各种各样的组合。我们希望这些相互配合的可能性，能够让多人游玩形成区别于单人模式的战斗体验，同时又不让独自游玩的玩家错过任何主要内容。
Q5. 《Turok: Origins》的视觉风格中存在一种有趣的反差：丛林、恐龙和古代遗迹等原始元素，与外星文明、未来武器及科幻装备同时出现在游戏中。团队在构建这些场景时，是如何让两种风格既保持各自的特点，又能自然地共存于同一个世界里的？
A：失落之地一直以来都充满了等待玩家发现的谜团与秘密，《Turok: Origins》也延续了这一特点。在整个战役过程中，玩家将前往多个不同的星球，而每个星球都有自己独特的动植物生态与历史背景。
为了塑造这些世界，概念设计团队与叙事团队进行了细致的规划，并参考了大量相关资料。我们希望这些环境在呈现出独特风貌的同时，也能让玩家感受到一种真实、可信的生命力。
与此同时，星际旅行的设定，以及玩家需要对抗强大外星敌人的故事背景，也为这些尚未被完全探索的环境注入了紧张感。玩家既可以在陌生的自然环境中探索与发现，也会在其中遭遇《Turok》系列一贯强调的激烈枪战。
我们希望通过这样的组合，让自然环境的神秘感与科幻战斗的紧张感彼此补充，共同构成《Turok: Origins》的世界。

members.title: Interview: RPG Maker U2U Lets You Build HD-2D Worlds Without Learning 3D

features.body:
Interview: RPG Maker U2U Lets You Build HD-2D Worlds Without Learning 3D
RPG Maker U2U Producer Hiroyuki Ichinose explains its P2D maps, atmospheric effects, reusable assets, standalone editor, and Lua plugins for accessible game development.
RPG Maker has spent decades lowering the barrier to game development, allowing solo creators and small teams to build complete projects without first becoming experienced programmers, technical artists, or engine specialists. RPG Maker U2U wants to preserve that accessibility while substantially expanding what its familiar tile-based workflow can produce.
Gotcha Gotcha Games has now released a free P2D Map Editor Demo on Steam, allowing users to experiment with the system before the complete development toolkit arrives. Maps created with the demo can be saved and transferred into the full release, although the current version is limited to map editing and does not include game-creation functionality. The demo is scheduled to remain available through November 16, 2026.
We spoke with RPG Maker U2U Producer Hiroyuki Ichinose about balancing visual freedom with approachability, reusing assets made for RPG Maker MV and MZ, adopting Luau for the new plugin system, and deliberately limiting camera movement to keep production manageable. Ichinose also discussed the difficult decision to discard and rebuild much of the original implementation so U2U could become a standalone Steam application, as well as the company’s response to criticism surrounding the closure and migration of the RPG Maker forums.
RPG Maker has always been known for making game development approachable. With RPG Maker U2U, how did the team think about preserving that ease of use while expanding what creators can make visually and structurally?
Hiroyuki Ichinose, Producer at Gotcha Gotcha Games: With every version of RPG Maker, we want everyone to be able to get started with game development easily. For U2U in particular, our highest priority is to keep the learning curve low and provide an environment that longtime users can feel right at home in.
That’s why we kept event creation, database editing, and other basic game-making workflows strongly based on their RPG Maker MZ versions. But we wanted to take a major step forward with what our maps can express.
So for U2U, we worked to make it so that, even without specialized knowledge of 3D, users can create maps with depth using a process that feels familiar to traditional tile placement.
U2U is based on the game-making experience of RPG Maker MZ, so returning RPG Maker users should recognize some of the interface and controls. How did the team decide what to preserve from previous RPG Maker tools and what needed to be redesigned?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: We made these decisions based on a simple principle: preserve the areas where users can build on their existing knowledge and experience, and only touch the parts needed to bring P2D (Perspective 2D) to life.
Event creation, database editing, and the basic UI and controls are basically the same, and build on the familiar game-making experience of RPG Maker MZ. Users can also reuse map tiles made for RPG Maker MV and MZ.
And since it’s a new system, we’ve designed the map editing system specifically for P2D. It will allow users to work intuitively with the newly added depth and height.
The new P2D map system seems like one of the biggest visual changes for U2U. Can you explain how it works and what kinds of depth, atmosphere, lighting, and presentation it allows creators to achieve?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: P2D (Perspective 2D) is a system for creating maps by turning traditional 2D map tiles into blocks placed in a 3D space. Even without specialized knowledge of 3D modeling, you can create maps with depth and height. It should be a process much like putting together building blocks.
With a 3D environment, we understand that some users may want to rotate the camera freely. However, allowing this would greatly increase the overall development workload, from learning the controls to building the assets and areas that remain unseen with a fixed camera.
That’s why we made the deliberate decision to leave out free camera rotation in U2U and have users build their maps around a specific camera angle. This allows us to introduce 3D visuals while preserving the ease of game creation that users expect from RPG Maker.
We’ve also included effects such as depth of field, cloud shadows, dust, heat haze, water surfaces, fog, light particles, and wind. By combining these effects, you can create scenes with depth and atmosphere while preserving the charm of pixel art.
How does U2U help users blend familiar 2D RPG Maker-style assets with a more modern 3D presentation? What should creators understand about building maps, scenes, and environments with this new approach?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: U2U uses the same map tile specifications as RPG Maker MV and MZ. By converting your existing MV and MZ 2D assets into P2D (Perspective 2D) blocks, you can reuse them in the P2D maps without having to redraw them, without depth or height restrictions.
When creating maps, you only need to focus on the areas visible from your chosen camera angle. This means you don’t need to model every part of an object, including the back, as you would in a typical 3D workflow.
We’ve also included over 100 ready-to-use P2D maps. You can use them as they are, or customize them while exploring how they’re put together. This lets you start with simple maps and add more detail as you become familiar with the tools. We hope they will also serve as good samples to learn from when getting started with creating wholly original maps.
RPG Maker is often associated with traditional story-driven RPGs, but creators have pushed the series in many different directions over the years. What kinds of games do you hope users will be able to create with U2U?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: We want creators to explore their ideas freely and make games without being limited to a particular genre.
With P2D (Perspective 2D), users can work with height differences and falling settings. These may open up possibilities for puzzles that make use of 3D space, or even action elements. However, we can’t promise at this stage that any particular genre or style of gameplay will be possible.
U2U also uses a new plugin system. In addition to plugins that expand game functionality, we plan to introduce “Editor Plugins” that expand the game-making environment itself. (※More details are provided below.) We hope that, as users create new plugins, they’ll find new ways to express their ideas in their games and customize their development environment to suit the games they want to make.
Just as with previous RPG Maker titles, we look forward to seeing games that go beyond anything we imagined during development.
From a visual-quality standpoint, what are the biggest improvements creators should notice when comparing U2U projects to games made in earlier RPG Maker tools?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: As you can imagine, the biggest difference is the addition of depth to maps.
With previous RPG Maker titles, maps were created on a flat 2D plane. With U2U, you can continue to use your existing pixel art while creating spaces with height differences, overpasses, underpasses, and so much more.
One example of the new features is a configurable heightmap, which lets you set ground height using shades of black and white. Lighter areas are higher, darker areas are lower, and gray represents the base height. We’ve included many features like this to help users create terrain with depth and height without having to learn specialized controls.
When combined with the new effects such as lighting, shadows, depth of field, fog, and water surfaces, you can create maps with much more atmosphere while still preserving the pixel art.
What kinds of built-in assets, visual tools, effects, or presentation features were most important for helping non-specialist creators make games that look polished?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: Our main priority was to make it easy to achieve a high quality look by providing assets and features right from the start, even without specialized knowledge.
Between character and monster illustrations, background music, sound effects, and over 100 ready-to-use P2D maps, there’s enough included assets to get any creator started.
Effects such as depth of field, fog, water surfaces, cloud shadows, and wind can be set up simply by choosing a preset and editing it. Fine adjustments to settings are easy to make, allowing users to create great-looking scenes just by creatively arranging the provided assets and combining effects, even without experience in 3D development or strong technical knowledge.
How is U2U approaching asset compatibility, and what should returning creators know about reusing or adapting their existing tiles, characters, animations, plugins, or project materials in this new engine?
Hiroyuki Ichinose: Compatibility varies depending on the type of asset.
With U2U, you can import map tiles from RPG Maker MV and MZ without any preparation or conversion and use them in P2D (Perspective 2D) maps. User-created map tiles can also be used, as long as they follow the same specifications.
Character images, face graphics, bust portraits, and background images can also be used just as in previous RPG Maker titles. We believe that being able to build on the assets users have collected over the years is an important part of making it easier to get started with game development.
However, existing projects cannot be transferred to U2U in their entirety due to project structure differences. Additionally, JavaScript plugins made for RPG Maker MV and MZ will not work as is. U2U uses Luau for its new plugin system; plugins will need to be created specifically for U2U.

features.rss_content: Got a complex game? Have you tried turning the tutorial into a 𝐫𝐞𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐝? Curiosity is one of the strongest drivers of human motivation. It can even override rationality and survival instincts. If you put a sign on a door that says “whatever you do, DO NOT OPEN THIS DOOR” we all know people are going to open the door. Skilled designers can weaponize this idea. Games with deep systems are immensely sticky and wildly satisfying, but trying to explain how the systems work AND what they give you as rewards AND why you should value those rewards is an immense amount of information for many games to hand out all at once… But without understanding what the rewards for this are and why they’re valuable, how will you get people to engage with them? Easy. Just don’t tell them what the reward is. Make it clear something is going to happen, probably something good… But don’t tell them what it is. Hollow Knight gives you rewards when you’ve hit certain collectible milestones, like with the Grubfather collecting his grubs. You don’t know what the reward’s going to be, but it doesn’t matter – as long as the rewards don’t disappoint us when we get them our curiosity will keep us motivated – and then make us interested in reading the text that explains the reward we just got. ai.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities
ai.summary_raw: Patch the Planet connects security researchers, maintainers, and incident responders to help address critical vulnerabilities across open source.

members.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities

ai.body:
Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to address critical vulnerabilities in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run websites and web applications. Calif identified a critical flaw using GPT‑5.6 Sol as part of our Patch the Planet(opens in a new window) initiative, with Wiz also independently discovering and reporting both vulnerabilities. PHP’s maintainers led the fixes and release, with our teams and partners like Wiz, Cloudflare, and others contributing research, technical support, and coordination to prepare protections ahead of disclosure.
For organizations using PHP, the priority now is applying the fixes. We’re sharing a PHP version checker as a Codex skill(opens in a new window) to help operators identify potentially vulnerable PHP versions and, alongside PHP’s and their providers’ guidance, determine which updates apply.
Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory. It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.
To our knowledge, frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did, opening a Defender’s Window for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure.
To help more defenders use these capabilities, we’ve committed $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access through Daybreak for Frontline Defenders, focused on organizations with limited security resources protecting essential services.
As significant as they are, these bugs are among several significant vulnerabilities we’ve already found and are working to fix, and we expect similar findings to increase sharply in the coming months. Drawing on our experience thus far, we’re sharing a proposed approach, appropriate for the AI era, to responding to critical vulnerabilities in widely used software, and we’re asking the security community to help improve this framework. It brings together our models, security expertise, and maintainers to help turn findings into protection and build a response that can scale as AI capabilities advance.
Getting a fix into use can mean adapting it for older releases, preparing provider mitigations, and updating systems across many organizations. A repeatable process helps those teams act quickly as more vulnerabilities are discovered.
Through Patch the Planet, we contributed security expertise and model access to support the PHP response, and worked with maintainers and research partners to test fixes and prepare guidance. We also helped coordinate with infrastructure providers on protections for affected systems and engaged government cyber agencies to help guidance reach critical organizations. This supported the maintainer-led response and helped other defenders prepare.
For some findings, researchers can work directly with the software’s maintainers to investigate the issue and develop a fix. Others need a wider response because they affect many products or because distributors and service providers need time (which may be in short supply if frontier capabilities are not too far ahead of those that are broadly available) to prepare updates and protections. In those cases, the proposed framework can help maintainers identify who needs to be involved and coordinate the work. The response can involve five stages:
Validate and fix the upstream vulnerability. The maintainer, researchers, and essential technical partners confirm the finding, assess its impact, and develop and test a fix. This process includes adversarial testing with frontier models to look for ways around the patch and related variants of the vulnerability.
Give affected organizations time to act. We propose a framework for considering which organizations need advance information to prepare protections, while maintainers decide whom to involve. We help with outreach, information-sharing agreements, and coordination between teams. A distributor might adapt a fix for an older release, a hosting provider might test a mitigation, and a security provider might prepare detection or prevention measures, including web application firewall (WAF) rules.
Coordinate with government partners to help protect critical systems. Government agencies play an essential role in coordinating a wider response and helping security guidance reach organizations responsible for critical infrastructure and other essential services. In the case of PHP, we worked, in collaboration with our partners, to engage with multiple parts of the U.S. government, including the White House’s Super Intelligence Force, the Office of the National Cyber Director (ONCD), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), as well as international partners to support that effort.
Prepare updates across affected products. As the fix, guidance, and disclosure plans become stable, maintainers can involve additional distributors, hosting and service providers, response teams, and operators to prepare updates and address gaps in coverage.
Once a patch is available, publish guidance and support deployment. Public guidance helps people assess their exposure, find authoritative updates or interim mitigations, and check that a fix is running. The response continues as operators deploy updates and report where they need help.
The proposed framework considers an organization’s protective role, including protecting its own systems and customers, the time needed to act, and its ability to handle sensitive information. The same criteria would apply to comparable organizations, with maintainers deciding whom to involve ahead of disclosure.
Each participant receives the information needed to carry out their protective work, from network logs with indicators of compromise to more sensitive working proof-of-concept exploits. Even limited details can reveal a vulnerability, so we weigh the risk of sharing them against the protection they enable.
Teams following this framework would work with maintainers to give defenders time to prepare and reassess the timeline if there’s active exploitation in the wild, a leak, a revealing public patch, or increased risk to users from stalled remediation.
The Patch the Planet website(opens in a new window) brings together public disclosures and guidance to help operators identify affected systems, find the right update, and verify that the updated software is running properly. For PHP, it points to the maintainers’ official patch and upgrade instructions and our partners’ technical research. The guidance also covers interim mitigations, when to involve a provider or expert, and backup and recovery. Interim protections can reduce risk, but we’ll make their limits and operational tradeoffs clear.
Operators can use CISA’s guidance on prioritization and remediation(opens in a new window) to assess how quickly to act based on exposure, exploitation, and potential impact. That may mean emergency patching, immediate mitigation, or a planned update, alongside forensic triage where warranted to assess whether systems have already been compromised. Priorities should be reassessed as conditions change, with a clear path to lasting remediation.
Global coordination depends on the people who maintain the software. Many projects are run by small teams that review security reports alongside routine development. Those teams need help separating new issues from duplicates, assessing impact, and testing fixes across supported releases. We support that work with funding, access to capable models, and hands-on engineering help.
Powerful AI capabilities are advancing across the industry, and we expect AI to play a growing role in helping defenders find vulnerabilities, monitor systems, and respond to threats. We’re investing in models, tools, and partnerships to help defenders put those capabilities to work.
Our investments include subscriptions for all maintainers through Codex for OSS and direct sponsorship of projects such as the Rust Foundation(opens in a new window) for maintainers and technical work. Each project sets its own priorities. Reusable tests and security workflows can reduce the effort needed to handle future findings. Open-source projects can apply to Patch the Planet(opens in a new window) for hands-on support.
We’re also calibrating additional blocking classifiers for Daybreak to help reduce the potential for misuse. This involves difficult tradeoffs: safeguards intended to prevent abuse can also block legitimate security work. Broad access to capable models and effective protections against misuse are both critical. Our aim is to preserve the capabilities defenders need to find and fix vulnerabilities while limiting harmful use. We’ll continue refining that balance as capabilities advance and we learn from how these tools are used.
As models become more capable, the opportunity extends beyond finding and fixing individual vulnerabilities. We want to help engineers build more secure software from the start. Improvements to a widely used component can prevent bugs or limit their impact across many products and services.
AI can help engineers understand existing code, prepare changes, and develop tests, while maintainers and security experts verify that those changes preserve the behavior users depend on. We see opportunities in several areas:
Secure code from the start. Coding models can help developers choose safer defaults, use security libraries correctly, and catch risky patterns as they write. Preventing vulnerabilities during development means fewer emergency fixes for maintainers and users.
